items.title: ms_components
items.text: ms_components is a set of reusable PySide6 widgets for MolSuite applications: SQLModel tables, a job monitor, a project browser, settings panels, a PyMOL dock, steppers, tool panels, and the shared theme.

items.title: Install
items.text:
ms_components requires Python 3.12. The base installation requires Qt; integrations are selected with extras:

pip install ms_components
pip install "ms_components[table,pymol]"
pip install "ms_components[all]"

The extras are table (SQLModel), monitor (Pydantic), projects (ms_flow), pymol (pymol-open-source alpha wheels), and steps (ms_env). dev adds all integrations and pytest. Extras change which dependencies are installed, not which component files are shipped.

Project widgets can use a supplied backend without ms_flow. The default catalog and python -m ms_components.ms_projects.app require the projects extra. The catalog creates its database on first use; a missing backend is reported with the installation command.

def add_condition(self, field: str, op: str, value: float, *, notify: bool = True) -> None:
    """Add (or replace) a condition: the same field+operator is an edit, not another chip."""
    if field not in self._labels or op not in dict(OPERATORS):
        return
    self._drop((field, op))
    self._conditions[(field, op)] = float(value)
    symbol = dict(OPERATORS)[op]
    chip = _Chip(field, op, f"{self._labels[field]} {symbol} {float(value):g}", self)
    chip.removed.connect(self._on_removed)
    self._chips[(field, op)] = chip
    self._row.insertWidget(self._row.count() - 1, chip)  # before the stretch
    self._empty.setVisible(False)
    if notify:
        self.changed.emit()

def set_conditions(self, conditions: Iterable[Condition]) -> None:
    """Whole state at once (restoring a saved view): a single signal."""
    for key in list(self._chips):

def set_external_clause(self, key: str, clause) -> None:
    """Overlay a raw SQLAlchemy clause under `key` (None removes it).

    Escape hatch for what FilterSpec cannot express - subqueries
    (`~exists(...)`), OR across fields, functions. It composes with AND just
    like `set_external_filters`, and because it is an already-built expression
    the builder does not interpret it: making sure it references the right
    model is the caller's responsibility.
    """
    if clause is None:
        self._external_clauses.pop(key, None)
    else:
        self._external_clauses[key] = clause
    self._page = 1

def all_ids(self) -> list[int]:
    """PKs of every row matching the current filters/search (no pagination).

    Lets a caller resolve "everything the table currently shows" into an id set
    without materializing rows. Honors filters + quick search, ignores paging.
    """
    pk = self._get_pk_attr()
    if pk is None:
        return []
    stmt = self._build_base_statement().with_only_columns(pk)
    with self._db.get_session() as session:
        # scalars(): with expr columns the base select has several entities and exec() yields Rows.
        return [int(value) for value in session.scalars(stmt).all() if value is not None]

def count(self) -> int:

    For hosts that want to keep the counter live (e.g. while a job inserts

def cursor_of(self, row: dict) -> tuple[Any, Any] | None:
    """Keyset cursor `(sort_value, pk)` for an already-loaded row."""
    raw = row.get("__raw__")
    pk = self._get_pk_attr()
    if raw is None or pk is None:
        return None
    pk_value = getattr(raw, pk.key, None)
    if not self._sorts:
        return (None, pk_value)
    sort = self._sorts[0]
    col_def = self._config.column_by_field(sort.field)
    key = col_def.display_key if col_def is not None else sort.field
    return ((row.get("__cursor_values__") or {}).get(key, row.get(key)), pk_value)

Next page by keyset: WHERE (sort, pk) > cursor, with no OFFSET.

OFFSET makes the engine walk and discard the previous N rows, so page 500 costs 500 times the first one. The cursor does not: it is always an index seek. The cursor is composite because the visible order is rarely unique (two identical scores).

def fetch_after(self, cursor: tuple[Any, Any] | None) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    """Next page by keyset: `WHERE (sort, pk) > cursor`, with no OFFSET.

    OFFSET makes the engine walk and discard the previous N rows, so page 500
    costs 500 times the first one. The cursor does not: it is always an index
    seek. The cursor is composite because the visible order is rarely unique
    (two identical scores).
    """
    stmt = self._build_base_statement()
    clause = self._keyset_clause(cursor)
    if clause is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(clause)
    with self._db.get_session() as session:
        total: int = session.exec(self._build_count_statement()).one()  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        rows = [self._row_to_dict(r) for r in session.exec(stmt.limit(self._page_size)).all()]
    return rows, total

def fetch_window_after(self, cursor: tuple[Any, Any] | None) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
    """The page after the cursor, without ``COUNT(*)``.

    Infinite scroll only needs to know whether another page exists. Asking for
    one extra row answers that without re-counting a potentially huge table on
    every move.
    """
    stmt = self._build_base_statement()
    clause = self._keyset_clause(cursor)
    if clause is not None:
        stmt = stmt.where(clause)
    with self._db.get_session() as session:
        raw = session.exec(stmt.limit(self._page_size + 1)).all()
    has_more = len(raw) > self._page_size
    return [self._row_to_dict(row) for row in raw[:self._page_size]], has_more

fetch_window_at(page_index: int, anchor: tuple[Any, Any] | None = None, anchor_page: int = 0) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]

Direct load for a scrollbar jump to a page that has not been walked yet.

anchor is the keyset cursor that starts anchor_page (None = the top). The walk from it to the target reads only (sort value, pk) - never whole rows - and then the page itself is a keyset seek, so jumping to the end of a 4M-row table no longer materializes 4M rows.

Source code in src/ms_components/ms_table/query_builder.py 
def fetch_window_at(self, page_index: int, anchor: tuple[Any, Any] | None = None,
                    anchor_page: int = 0) -> tuple[list[dict], bool]:
    """Direct load for a scrollbar jump to a page that has not been walked yet.

    `anchor` is the keyset cursor that starts `anchor_page` (None = the top). The
    walk from it to the target reads only (sort value, pk) - never whole rows -
    and then the page itself is a keyset seek, so jumping to the end of a 4M-row
    table no longer materializes 4M rows.
    """
    offset = max(0, int(page_index) - int(anchor_page)) * self._page_size
    if self._get_pk_attr() is None:  # no keyset possible: plain OFFSET
        stmt = self._build_base_statement().offset(int(page_index) * self._page_size)
        with self._db.get_session() as session:
            raw = session.exec(stmt.limit(self._page_size + 1)).all()
        return [self._row_to_dict(row) for row in raw[:self._page_size]], len(raw) > self._page_size
    cursor = self._seek(anchor, offset) if offset else anchor
    if offset and cursor is None:
        return [], False  # past the end (rows vanished under the scrollbar)
    return self.fetch_window_after(cursor)

def fetch(self) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    """Run the query and return (rows_as_dicts, total_count)."""
    with self._db.get_session() as session:
        total: int = session.exec(self._build_count_statement()).one()  # type: ignore[arg-type]

    rows, _has_more = self.fetch_window_at(self._page - 1)
    return rows, total

to_query_spec() -> dict

The "filtered" selection as QuerySpec kwargs, ready to hand to a job.

Returns a dict rather than a QuerySpec so the table does not take ms_flow as a dependency; the host does QuerySpec(**builder.to_query_spec()). This is what avoids materialising a list of ids: the job receives the query, not its result.

Raises when any part of the current state is not expressible (expression columns, LIKE/ILIKE filters over joins): staying quiet and sending a wider query would be worse.

def to_query_spec(self) -> dict:
    """The "filtered" selection as QuerySpec kwargs, ready to hand to a job.

    Returns a dict rather than a QuerySpec so the table does not take ms_flow as
    a dependency; the host does `QuerySpec(**builder.to_query_spec())`. This is
    what avoids materialising a list of ids: the job receives the query, not its
    result.

    Raises when any part of the current state is not expressible (expression
    columns, LIKE/ILIKE filters over joins): staying quiet and sending a wider
    query would be worse.
    """
    model = self._config.model_class
    table = getattr(getattr(model, "__table__", None), "name", "") or model.__name__.lower()

    filters: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for f in self._all_filters():
        col_def = self._config.column_by_field(f.field)
        if col_def is not None and col_def.expr is not None:
            raise ValueError(f"Column '{f.field}' filters on a SQL expression; QuerySpec cannot carry it.")
        if "." in f.field:
            raise ValueError(f"Filter on joined field '{f.field}' has no QuerySpec equivalent.")
        if f.op in (FilterOperator.LIKE, FilterOperator.ILIKE):
            filters[f"{f.field}__contains"] = str(f.value).strip("%")
            continue
        suffix = self._SPEC_OPS.get(f.op)
        if suffix is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Filter operator {f.op} has no QuerySpec equivalent.")
        filters[f"{f.field}{suffix}"] = f.value

    if self._external_clauses:
        raise ValueError("Raw SQLAlchemy clauses set by the host cannot be exported to QuerySpec.")
    if self._search_text and self._search_fields:
        # Quick search is an OR across columns; QuerySpec filters are ANDed.
        raise ValueError("Quick search (OR across columns) has no QuerySpec equivalent.")

    order = tuple(
        f"-{s.field}" if s.descending else s.field
        for s in self._sorts
        if "." not in s.field
    )
    return {"table": table, "filters": filters, "order": order}

def ensure_viewport_filled(self, *, force: bool = False) -> bool:
    """One tick of a job's start-up: reload rows only once there are enough to
    fill the visible viewport (or once the host decides it has waited long
    enough, force=True).

    Returns True when the viewport is full (or there is nothing else to fetch):
    the host then switches to "counters only" mode. False = still waiting, call
    again.
    """
    loaded = self._model.loaded_count
    capacity = self._viewport_row_capacity()
    if loaded >= capacity:
        return True
    total = self._builder.count()
    if not force and total < capacity:
        return False  # not enough molecules yet to fill the view
    if total <= loaded:
        return force
    self.refresh()
    return force or self._model.loaded_count >= capacity

def patch_loaded_rows(self, key: str, patches: dict[Any, dict[str, Any]]) -> bool:
    """Patch visible cached rows by a raw-object/key value; no model reset or reselection."""
    changed = False
    for row in self._model.loaded_rows:
        data = self._model.get_row_data(row) or {}
        raw = data.get("__raw__")
        identity = data.get(key, getattr(raw, key, None))
        values = patches.get(identity)
        if values is not None:
            changed = self._model.patch_loaded_row(row, values) or changed
    return changed

def set_toolbar_actions(self, key: str, actions: list[ToolbarAction]) -> None:
    """Put a host's commands on this table's toolbar while it needs them.

    Same shape as `set_external_filters`: keyed by the host (a tool id), replacing
    whatever that key had, and an empty list is `clear_toolbar_actions(key)`. A tool that
    narrows a table can now also act on it, and gives both back on the way out.
    """
    self.clear_toolbar_actions(key)
    if not actions:
        return
    if self._toolbar is None:
        # Config asked for no toolbar; a runtime action still has to be reachable.
        self.layout().insertWidget(0, self._build_toolbar())
    added = [self._make_action(a) for a in actions]
    for act in added:
        act.setVisible(not self._actions_collapsed)
        self._toolbar.insertAction(self._zone_anchor, act)
    self._keyed_actions[key] = added

def apply_view_state(self, state: dict | None) -> None:
    """Apply a previously saved view_state(). Unknown fields are ignored;
    an empty/missing 'columns' leaves the config-defined visibility intact."""
    if not state:
        return
    columns = state.get("columns")
    if columns:
        wanted = set(columns)
        known = {c.field for c in self._config.columns}
        # Only apply if it references real columns; keep at least one visible.
        if wanted & known:
            for c in self._config.columns:
                c.visible = c.field in wanted
    sort = state.get("sort")
    if sort:
        self._builder.set_sort(
            [SortSpec(s["field"], descending=bool(s.get("descending"))) for s in sort if s.get("field")]
        )
    self._install_delegates()
    self._sync_header()
    self.refresh()

def refresh(self, reset_page: bool = True) -> None:
    """Reload data from the DB with the current filter/sort/page state."""
    if self._is_infinite_mode():
        self._builder.set_page(1)
        self._new_generation()
        # The first page stays on this thread (hosts select it right after refresh());
        # it is a keyset seek. The COUNT is what costs at millions of rows.
        rows, has_more = self._builder.fetch_window_after(None)
        self._infinite_pages = {0: rows}
        self._infinite_page_cursors = {0: None}
        if rows:
            self._infinite_page_cursors[1] = self._builder.cursor_of(rows[-1])
        self._infinite_frontier_page = 0
        self._infinite_loaded_end = len(rows)
        self._infinite_has_more = has_more
        self._infinite_total_hint = len(rows) + int(has_more)
        self._infinite_total_exact = not has_more
        self._model.load_data(
            rows,
            self._infinite_total_hint,
            1,
            window_start=0,
            total_is_exact=self._infinite_total_exact,
        )
        # New rows from the top: a scrollbar left deep down would jump to a page of a
        # query that no longer exists.
        self._table.verticalScrollBar().setValue(0)
        if has_more:
            self._run_async(self._builder.count, self._apply_count)
        return
    if reset_page:
        self._builder.set_page(1)

    rows, total = self._builder.fetch()
    self._model.load_data(rows, total, self._builder.current_page)

def set_total(self, total: int) -> None:
    """Update only the total (counters/pagination), leaving loaded rows alone."""
    new_total = max(0, int(total))
    old_total = self.rowCount()
    if self._config.load_mode == TableLoadMode.INFINITE and new_total > old_total:
        self.beginInsertRows(QModelIndex(), old_total, new_total - 1)
        self._total = new_total
        self.endInsertRows()
    elif self._config.load_mode == TableLoadMode.INFINITE and new_total < old_total:
        self.beginRemoveRows(QModelIndex(), new_total, old_total - 1)
        self._total = new_total
        self.endRemoveRows()
    else:
        self._total = new_total
    self._total_is_exact = True
    self.data_loaded.emit(self._total, self._page)

def patch_loaded_row(self, row: int, values: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    """Change displayed values in one loaded row without resetting selection or scroll."""
    row_data = self.get_row_data(row)
    if row_data is None:
        return False
    changed_columns: list[int] = []
    offset = 1 if self._config.show_row_numbers else 0
    for column, col_def in enumerate(self._visible_cols, start=offset):
        key = col_def.display_key
        if key in values and row_data.get(key) != values[key]:
            row_data[key] = values[key]
            changed_columns.append(column)
    if not changed_columns:
        return False
    self.dataChanged.emit(
        self.index(row, min(changed_columns)),
        self.index(row, max(changed_columns)),
        [Qt.DisplayRole],
    )
    return True

def describe_host(address: str, env: str = "", packages=(), tools=None) -> str:
    """What the machine `address` (empty: this one) is and has, in a few lines: its system, CPUs,
    memory and GPUs, the Python of `env` there with the version of each of `packages`, and whether
    each of `tools` (name -> path) can be run. One `ssh` call, which raises `HostError` when it does
    not get in. Blocks: not on the GUI thread."""
    from ms_env import Host

    tools = tools or {}
    python = f"{env.rstrip('/')}/bin/python" if env else ("" if address else sys.executable)
    script = "; ".join([
        "export LC_ALL=C", "uname -srm", '(. /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null && echo "$PRETTY_NAME")',
        'echo "CPUs: $(nproc 2>/dev/null || sysctl -n hw.ncpu)"',
        "awk '/MemTotal/ {printf \"Memory: %.1f GB\\n\", $2/1048576}' /proc/meminfo 2>/dev/null",
        "(nvidia-smi -L 2>/dev/null || echo 'GPUs: none seen by nvidia-smi')",
        "echo",
        *([f"if [ -x {shlex.quote(python)} ]; then {shlex.quote(python)} -c {shlex.quote(_VERSIONS)} "
           f"{' '.join(map(shlex.quote, packages))}; else echo 'Environment: none at '{shlex.quote(python)}; fi"]
          if python else ["echo 'Environment: none named; the app prepares one before the first job'"]),
        *(f"([ -x {shlex.quote(path)} ] && echo '  ✓ {name} '{shlex.quote(path)} || echo '  ✗ {name} not found at '{shlex.quote(path)})"
          for name, path in tools.items()),
    ])
    if tools:
        script = script.replace("; ([ -x", "; echo 'Tools:'; ([ -x", 1)
    began = time.monotonic()
    said = Host(address or None).run(script, timeout=60).decode(errors="replace").strip()
    return f"Connected to {address or 'this machine'} in {time.monotonic() - began:.1f} s\n\n{said}"

items.title: PyMOL
items.text:
Comparison scenes provide grid and overlay layouts without reloading structures or changing the camera. Assign each structure/pose pair the same positive PyMOL grid_slot, then pass its display name:

dock.set_scene_context(
    "comparison",
    grid_labels={1: "Complex A", 3: "Complex B"},
)
dock.set_comparison_layout("overlay")

grid_labels is also accepted by PymolControlBar and PymolSceneContext. Without explicit labels, molecular object titles (or object names when no title is available) are joined per positive grid_slot within the context's target. Applications must pass display names if those names are not present in PyMOL.

The Display > Comparison > Grid / Overlay menu appears only in comparison scenes. The chosen layout persists when changing poses or applying presets. Overlay displays the existing coordinates together; alignment remains the caller's responsibility.

Each label is a pseudoatom named panel_text<slot>, initially sized 14. Grid labels appear at the top-left of their panel; overlay labels form a stacked legend that follows viewport resizing. Receptor cartoons, carbon atoms and label text share the slot's COMPARISON_COLORS color. Heteroatom colors are preserved. The label outline uses PyMOL's background-adaptive front color for readability on light and dark backgrounds. The palette has ten colors and repeats beyond ten slots. Existing labels are updated in place, so individual settings remain editable, for example cmd.set("label_size", 18, "panel_text3"). Presets restore label visibility after changing molecular representations.

To replace one pose without rebuilding the scene, pass its bytes directly:

dock.replace_comparison_object(
    "pose_a", pdb_bytes, "pdb",
    reference="receptor_a", label="Complex A [P2]",
)

The new object inherits the reference's transformation and slot, is shown as sticks, and receives the same comparison color. Camera and auto-zoom settings are preserved. The previous object remains available until the replacement loads successfully. This API neither fetches data nor calls the hosting application. Hosts remain responsible for reading their data and discarding stale requests.

Setting any non-comparison scene context after a comparison context removes the managed labels and sets grid_mode to zero. Applications should update the scene context when leaving their off-target view, even without loading a new structure. Unrelated grid scenes and user-created annotations are not removed. "offtarget" remains accepted as an alias for "comparison".

def add_scene_actions(
    menu: QMenu,
    dock,
    *,
    color_role: Callable[[object, str, str], None] | None = None,
) -> QMenu:
    """Append Background, Camera, Render, Surface, Complex and the internal-GUI toggle to `menu`.

    `color_role(cmd, selection, role)` colors the protein ("receptor") and ligand ("ligand")
    in the Complex actions; the default is carbons by role, heteroatoms by element."""
    color_role = color_role or _default_color_role
    parent = menu.parentWidget() if isinstance(menu.parentWidget(), QWidget) else None

    def run(label: str, work: Callable[[object], None]) -> Callable[[], None]:
        def handler() -> None:
            cmd = getattr(dock, "cmd", None)
            if cmd is None:
                return
            try:
                work(cmd)
            except Exception as exc:
                QMessageBox.warning(parent, "PyMOL", f"Could not {label}:\n{exc}")
        return handler

    def complex_selections(cmd) -> tuple[str, str]:
        protein, ligand = "ms_complex_protein", "ms_complex_ligand"
        select_atoms(cmd, protein, "polymer.protein")
        if not select_atoms(cmd, ligand, "organic and not solvent"):
            select_atoms(cmd, ligand, "not polymer.protein and not solvent")
        return protein, ligand

    def protein_ligand(cmd) -> None:
        protein, ligand = complex_selections(cmd)
        cmd.hide("everything", "all")
        cmd.show("cartoon", protein)
        cmd.show("sticks", ligand)
        color_role(cmd, protein, "receptor")
        color_role(cmd, ligand, "ligand")
        cmd.show("lines", "solvent")
        cmd.set("cartoon_transparency", 0.12, protein)
        cmd.zoom(ligand, 5)

    def focus_ligand(cmd) -> None:
        _protein, ligand = complex_selections(cmd)
        cmd.show("sticks", ligand)
        cmd.zoom(ligand, 4)
        cmd.orient(ligand)

    def pocket(cmd) -> None:
        protein, ligand = complex_selections(cmd)
        name = "ms_complex_pocket"
        cmd.select(name, f"byres ({protein} within 5 of {ligand})")
        cmd.show("sticks", name)
        color_role(cmd, name, "receptor")
        cmd.show("surface", name)
        cmd.set("transparency", 0.55, name)
        cmd.zoom(f"({name} or {ligand})", 4)

    def save_png(cmd) -> None:
        filename, _filter = QFileDialog.getSaveFileName(
            parent, "Save PyMOL Image", str(Path.home() / "pymol.png"), "PNG Images (*.png)"
        )
        if filename:
            cmd.png(filename, ray=1)

    background = menu.addMenu("Background")
    for label, color in (("White", "white"), ("Black", "black"), ("Grey", "grey20")):
        menu_action(background, label, run("set the background", lambda cmd, c=color: cmd.bg_color(c)))

    camera = menu.addMenu("Camera")
    menu_action(camera, "Orthoscopic", run("set the camera", lambda cmd: cmd.set("orthoscopic", 1)))
    menu_action(camera, "Perspective", run("set the camera", lambda cmd: cmd.set("orthoscopic", 0)))

    render = menu.addMenu("Render")
    menu_action(render, "Shadows On", run("set shadows", lambda cmd: cmd.set("ray_shadows", 1)))
    menu_action(render, "Shadows Off", run("set shadows", lambda cmd: cmd.set("ray_shadows", 0)))
    menu_action(render, "Ray", run("ray-trace", lambda cmd: cmd.ray()))
    menu_action(render, "Save PNG…", run("save the PNG", save_png))

    surface = menu.addMenu("Surface")
    menu_action(surface, "Vacuum Electrostatics…", lambda: _vacuum_electrostatics(dock, parent),
                tooltip="Generate a charge-colored surface (Generate > Vacuum electrostatics). Slow.")

    complex_menu = menu.addMenu("Complex")
    menu_action(complex_menu, "Protein–Ligand", run("apply the protein-ligand view", protein_ligand),
                tooltip="Protein cartoon, ligand sticks, ligand-focused camera.")
    menu_action(complex_menu, "Focus Ligand", run("focus the ligand", focus_ligand))
    menu_action(complex_menu, "Pocket", run("show the pocket", pocket),
                tooltip="Residues within 5 Å of the ligand as sticks + transparent surface.")

    menu.addSeparator()
    gui = menu.addAction("PyMOL Internal GUI")
    gui.setCheckable(True)
    gui.setChecked(False)  # the dock starts with internal_gui off
    gui.setToolTip("Show or hide PyMOL's built-in on-canvas menu/object panel.")
    gui.toggled.connect(lambda checked: _internal_gui(dock, checked))
    return menu

frame(cmd, selection: str, buffer: float = 2.0) -> None

Move the camera so selection fits the panel in both directions. PyMOL's zoom fits the height only, so a tall, narrow panel cuts the sides off.

Source code in src/ms_components/ms_pymol/scene.py 
def frame(cmd, selection: str, buffer: float = 2.0) -> None:
    """Move the camera so `selection` fits the panel in both directions. PyMOL's zoom fits the
    height only, so a tall, narrow panel cuts the sides off."""
    import numpy as np

    xyz = cmd.get_coords(selection)
    width, height = cmd.get_viewport()
    if xyz is None or width <= 0 or height <= 0:
        return
    view = list(cmd.get_view())
    camera = (xyz - np.asarray(view[12:15])) @ np.reshape(view[:9], (3, 3))  # model -> camera axes
    half_x, half_y = np.abs(camera[:, :2]).max(axis=0) + buffer
    tan = math.tan(math.radians(float(cmd.get("field_of_view")) / 2))
    distance = float(max(half_y, half_x * height / width) / tan + np.abs(camera[:, 2]).max())
    shift = distance - abs(view[11])
    view[11] = -distance  # negative: the camera looks down -z at the origin
    view[15] += shift  # the clipping planes are measured from the camera
    view[16] += shift
    cmd.set_view(view)

set_scene_context(dock, kind: str, *, target: str = 'all', selections: dict[str, str] | None = None, default_preset: str = '', restore_view: bool = True, grid_labels: dict[int, str] | None = None, complex_preset: str = '') -> None

Set the dock's scene context, then restore the molecule's remembered style and view.

In an additive scene the roles of the previous context are kept: a pair of receptor and ligand becomes a "complex" (with complex_preset), a comparison grows a grid slot per new object. restore_view=False keeps the camera the caller just set.

Source code in src/ms_components/ms_pymol/scene.py 
def set_scene_context(
    dock,
    kind: str,
    *,
    target: str = "all",
    selections: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    default_preset: str = "",
    restore_view: bool = True,
    grid_labels: dict[int, str] | None = None,
    complex_preset: str = "",
) -> None:
    """Set the dock's scene context, then restore the molecule's remembered style and view.

    In an additive scene the roles of the previous context are kept: a pair of receptor and
    ligand becomes a "complex" (with `complex_preset`), a comparison grows a grid slot per new
    object. `restore_view=False` keeps the camera the caller just set."""
    if is_additive(dock):
        cmd = dock.cmd
        previous = getattr(dock, "scene_context", None)
        if previous is not None and not any(object_list(cmd, s) for s in previous.selections.values()):
            previous = None
        roles = dict(selections or {})
        if previous is not None:
            for role, selection in previous.selections.items():
                names = object_list(cmd, selection)
                names.extend(object_list(cmd, roles.get(role, "none")))
                if names:
                    roles[role] = " or ".join(dict.fromkeys(names))
        selections = roles
        objects = list(dict.fromkeys(obj for selection in roles.values() for obj in object_list(cmd, selection)))
        replaced_slots = getattr(dock, "_scene_replaced_slots", {})
        for obj in objects:
            if obj in replaced_slots:
                cmd.set("grid_slot", replaced_slots.pop(obj), obj)
        target = " or ".join(objects) or target
        if (previous is not None and previous.is_comparison) or kind in {"comparison", "offtarget"}:
            kind = "comparison"
            grid_labels = {**(dict(previous.grid_labels) if previous is not None else {}), **(grid_labels or {})}
            slots = {obj: cmd.get_setting_int("grid_slot", obj) for obj in objects}
            unassigned = [obj for obj, slot in slots.items() if slot <= 0]
            if unassigned:
                slot = max([0, *slots.values()]) + 1
                for obj in unassigned:
                    cmd.set("grid_slot", slot, obj)
                grid_labels[slot] = " + ".join(unassigned)
        elif "receptor" in roles and "ligand" in roles:
            kind, default_preset = "complex", complex_preset
        elif len(roles) > 1:
            kind, default_preset = "generic", ""
    setter = getattr(dock, "set_scene_context", None)
    if callable(setter):
        setter(kind, target=target, selections=selections, default_preset=default_preset, grid_labels=grid_labels)
    memory = getattr(dock, "scene_memory", None)
    if memory is not None:
        memory.apply(kind, target, selections, restore_view=restore_view)
    if is_additive(dock) and kind not in {"comparison", "offtarget"}:
        dock.cmd.zoom(target, 3)

def __init__(self, folder: Path, molblock: str, *, title: str, note: str = "", parent=None):
    from PySide6.QtWebEngineWidgets import QWebEngineView  # heavy: only when someone edits

def run_editor(
    folder: Path,
    molblock: str,
    title: str,
    *,
    note: str = "",
    theme: str = "auto",
    base_font_pt: float | None = None,
) -> str | None:
    """Open a KetcherDialog in a child process and wait; the drawing after Apply, None on Cancel.
    Blocking: call it off the GUI thread. `theme`/`base_font_pt` go to ms_components.theme."""
    options = {"folder": str(folder), "title": title, "note": note, "theme": theme, "base_font_pt": base_font_pt}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        out = Path(tmp) / "edited.mol"
        proc = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", __name__, json.dumps(options), str(out)],
            input=molblock, capture_output=True, text=True,
        )
        if proc.returncode != 0:
            raise RuntimeError(f"The editor stopped (exit code {proc.returncode}):\n{proc.stderr[-2000:]}")
        return out.read_text() if out.exists() else None

Reusable stepper component for PySide6, modelled on Quasar's (https://quasar.dev/vue-components/stepper).

It provides
  • A header with indicators (number / prefix / icon / check / error) and connectors. HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL orientation (inline content).
  • Per-step states: inactive, active, done and error.
  • alternative-labels (horizontal): title/caption centred under the indicator. inline-label (vertical): title next to the indicator.
  • prefix: short text inside the indicator instead of the number.
  • Per-state icons: done / active / error, global and per step.
  • Per-step colours (active / done / inactive / error) over the base theme.
  • Validation hooks: each step may carry a validator that blocks advancing and marks the step as failed.
  • Programmatic navigation (next / previous / go_to) and header clicks (configurable per step).
  • Optional navigation bar (Back / Continue / Finish).
  • QSS-style theming: painted colours exposed as qproperty-*, and chrome (buttons, connectors, background) styleable by objectName. Example themes: light, dark, outlined and flat.
  • Signals: current_changed, step_changed, finished, validation_failed.

def next(self) -> None:
    """Validate the current step and, if it passes, mark it done and advance."""
    if not self._leave_current_ok():

def start(self, tutorial: Tutorial):
    """Validate bindings before replacing the active tour. Must run in the UI thread."""
    for step in tutorial.steps:
        if self.close_only and step.advance_on is None:
            raise ValueError("Close-only tutorials require an event for every step")
        if not isinstance(self.targets.get(step.target), TutorialTarget):
            raise ValueError(f"Unregistered tutorial target: {step.target}")
        if step.advance_on is not None and not isinstance(self.events.get(step.advance_on), TutorialEvent):
            raise ValueError(f"Unregistered tutorial event: {step.advance_on}")
    app = QApplication.instance()
    if app is None:
        raise RuntimeError("TutorialController requires a QApplication")
    self.stop()
    focus = app.focusWidget()
    self._previous_focus = weakref.ref(focus) if focus is not None else None
    self._tutorial = tutorial
    self._completed.clear()
    app.installEventFilter(self)
    self._tracker.start()
    self.started.emit(tutorial.id)
    if self._tutorial is tutorial:
        self._show_step(0)

@Slot()
def refresh(self):
    """Resolve the current target and instructions after an application UI change."""
    step = self.current_step
    if step is None:
        return
    try:
        source = self.targets[step.target].widget
        target = source() if callable(source) else source
        if not isinstance(target, QWidget) or not isValid(target):
            raise ValueError(f"Target '{step.target}' is unavailable")
        self._target = target
        if not target.isVisible():
            if self.overlay is not None:
                self.overlay.hide()
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Target '{step.target}' is hidden; provide a prepare callback")
            return
        host = target.window()
        if self.overlay is None or self.overlay.parentWidget() is not host:
            if self.overlay is not None:
                self.overlay.hide()
                self.overlay.deleteLater()
            self._overlay = TutorialOverlay(host, dim_background=self.dim_background, close_only=self.close_only)
            self._overlay.next_requested.connect(self.next)
            self._overlay.back_requested.connect(self.back)
            self._overlay.exit_requested.connect(self.stop)
            self.destroyed.connect(self._overlay.deleteLater)
        if self.overlay.step is not step:
            self.overlay.set_step(self._tutorial.title, step, self._index, len(self._tutorial.steps))
        if self.instruction_provider is not None:
            self.overlay.set_text(self.instruction_provider(step))
        self.overlay.next_button.setEnabled(step.advance_on is None or step.id in self._completed)
        region = self.targets[step.target].rect
        self.overlay.reposition(target, interactive=step.advance_on is not None,
                                rect=region() if region is not None else None)
    except Exception as exc:
        self._fail(f"Cannot resolve tutorial step '{step.id}': {exc}")

def load_tutorial(path: str | Path) -> Tutorial:
    """Read data only: target/event names are resolved by the application, never evaluated."""
    with Path(path).open("rb") as source:
        data = tomllib.load(source)
    allowed = {"id", "title", "steps"}
    if set(data) - allowed:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown tutorial keys: {', '.join(sorted(set(data) - allowed))}")
    if not isinstance(data.get("steps"), list):
        raise ValueError("Tutorial must contain [[steps]] tables")
    try:
        return Tutorial(id=data["id"], title=data["title"],
                        steps=tuple(TutorialStep(**step) for step in data["steps"]))
    except (KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise ValueError(f"Invalid tutorial definition: {exc}") from exc

def set_progress(
    self,
    done: int,
    total: int | None = None,
    *,
    stage: str = "Running",
    unit: str = "items",
    eta_seconds: float | None = None,
    failures: int = 0,
    detail: str = "",
) -> None:
    """``eta_seconds=None`` estimates it from the rate observed across calls.
    ``total=None`` keeps the line indeterminate and drops the ETA: a streamed total is
    only a floor, so a percentage would be invented. ``detail`` follows the ETA."""
    self._set_running(True)
    parts = []
    if total:
        self.progress.setRange(0, int(total))
        self.progress.setValue(min(done, int(total)))
        headline = f"{stage} — {format_count(done)} / {format_count(total)} {unit}"
        if eta_seconds is None:
            eta_seconds = self._estimate_eta(done, int(total))
        parts.append("Estimating time…" if eta_seconds is None else format_eta(eta_seconds))
    else:
        self.progress.setRange(0, 0)
        headline = f"{stage} — {format_count(done)} {unit}"
    if detail:
        parts.append(detail)
    self._show(headline, " · ".join(parts), failures)

items.text:
Color themes for every MolSuite Qt app (QPalette-based).

Palette data is derived from qt-themes by Beat Reichenbach, MIT-licensed:

https://github.com/beatreichenbach/qt-themes
Copyright (c) 2024 Beat Reichenbach

The color values are vendored here (they are data, not code) so no extra runtime dependency is needed. Full MIT text: licenses/qt-themes-LICENSE.txt; keep this attribution if you redistribute.

Widgets should not hardcode colors. Two mechanisms cover everything:

  • palette(role) in QSS / QApplication.palette() in paint code — resolved live, so a theme switch repaints without touching a single widget.
  • color("red"/"green"/...) for semantic accents (status dots, warnings) that have no QPalette role.

Same idea for type: font(role) derives from the app font instead of hardcoding sizes, so the OS/user font and DPI carry through. Roles are data (FONT_ROLES), not classes -- a title is a scale factor and a weight, nothing worth an object.

def contrast_ratio(left: QColor, right: QColor) -> float:
    """WCAG contrast ratio used to keep generated palette states readable."""

def font(role: str = "body", *, mono: bool = False) -> QFont:
    """A QFont for a named role, derived from the application font.

    `mono=True` swaps in the platform's fixed-width family (scores, ids, paths) and
    keeps the role's size/weight.
    """
    app = QApplication.instance()
    base = app.font() if app is not None else QFont()
    scale, bold = FONT_ROLES.get(role, FONT_ROLES["body"])
    result = QFontDatabase.systemFont(QFontDatabase.FixedFont) if mono else QFont(base)
    if base.pointSizeF() > 0:  # a font set in pixels reports -1 here
        result.setPointSizeF(base.pointSizeF() * scale)
    else:
        result.setPixelSize(max(1, round(base.pixelSize() * scale)))
    result.setBold(bold)
    return result

Set the application base font: the root everything else inherits from.

One place instead of sizes scattered through the QSS: font(role) scales off this one, widgets that do not override it inherit it, and the QSS can go without a single font-size rule (a stylesheet rule would override this).

def set_base_font(points: float = DEFAULT_FONT_PT, *, family: str | None = None,
                  app: QApplication | None = None) -> QFont:
    """Set the application base font: the root everything else inherits from.

    One place instead of sizes scattered through the QSS: `font(role)` scales off this
    one, widgets that do not override it inherit it, and the QSS can go without a single
    `font-size` rule (a stylesheet rule would override this).

    Call it before creating windows: widgets already built with their own font keep it.
    """
    app = app or QApplication.instance()
    if app is None:
        raise RuntimeError("set_base_font requires a running QApplication")
    result = QFont(app.font())
    if family:  # by default the system family is kept and only the size is set
        result.setFamily(family)
    result.setPointSizeF(float(points))
    app.setFont(result)
    return result

def build_palette(theme: dict[str, str]) -> QPalette:
    """Build a QPalette from a theme dict: one key per role, plus the Disabled text."""
    Role = QPalette.ColorRole
    Group = QPalette.ColorGroup
    pal = QPalette()
    for key, role in _ROLES.items():
        pal.setColor(role, QColor(theme[key]))  # all groups; Disabled is overridden below
    disabled = QColor(theme["disabled_text"])
    for role in (Role.WindowText, Role.Text, Role.ButtonText, Role.PlaceholderText, Role.BrightText,
                 Role.HighlightedText, Role.Link, Role.LinkVisited, Role.Accent):
        pal.setColor(Group.Disabled, role, disabled)
    for role in (Role.Base, Role.AlternateBase, Role.Button):
        pal.setColor(Group.Disabled, role, QColor(theme["window"]))
    pal.setColor(Group.Disabled, Role.Highlight, QColor(theme["mid"]))
    return pal

tone_qss(theme: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str

QProgressBar[tone="green"], QLabel[tone="blue"] and siblings, from the live theme.

QSS has no palette role for the accents, so these rules are written per theme. Bars are translucent, so their text stays readable on dark and light themes alike; labels take the hue as text (every hue is >= 4.5:1 on the theme's surfaces).

Source code in src/ms_components/theme.py 
def tone_qss(theme: dict[str, str] | None = None) -> str:
    """`QProgressBar[tone="green"]`, `QLabel[tone="blue"]` and siblings, from the live theme.

    QSS has no palette role for the accents, so these rules are written per theme.
    Bars are translucent, so their text stays readable on dark and light themes alike;
    labels take the hue as text (every hue is >= 4.5:1 on the theme's surfaces).
    """
    theme = theme or _current
    rules = []
    for tone in TONES:
        accent = QColor(theme[tone])
        rgba = f"rgba({accent.red()}, {accent.green()}, {accent.blue()}, 150)"
        rules.append(f'QProgressBar[tone="{tone}"]::chunk {{ background: {rgba}; }}')
    rules += [f'QLabel[tone="{hue}"] {{ color: {theme[hue]}; }}' for hue in HUES]
    return "\n".join(rules) + "\n"

def apply_theme(name: str, app: QApplication | None = None, *,
                base_font_pt: float | None = None) -> None:
    """Apply a theme (or "auto") to the QApplication.

    Re-applies live to every existing widget. Non-Qt "islands" (PyMOL, pyqtgraph)
    do not observe this and must be pushed separately.
    """
    global _current
    app = app or QApplication.instance()
    if app is None:
        raise RuntimeError("apply_theme requires a running QApplication")
    _current = THEMES[resolve(name)]
    if base_font_pt is not None:  # optional: omit it and the system font stays
        set_base_font(base_font_pt, app=app)
    if not isinstance(app.style(), _EdgedFusion):
        app.setStyle(_EdgedFusion())  # Fusion honors QPalette ColorRoles most faithfully
    app.setPalette(build_palette(_current))
    app.setStyleSheet(base_qss() + tone_qss())

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication, QComboBox, QPushButton, QSpinBox

from ms_components.theme import apply_theme
from ms_components.tool_panel import ToolPanel

app = QApplication([])
apply_theme("auto", app)

panel = ToolPanel()
options = panel.add_section("Options")
engine = QComboBox()
engine.addItems(["vina", "vinardo"])
options.add_row("Scoring function", engine)
options.add_row("Exhaustiveness", QSpinBox(value=8))
panel.advanced.add_row("Seed", QSpinBox())

total = 50
state = {"done": 0}
bar = panel.action_bar
bar.set_summary(f"{total} ligands selected")
run_button = QPushButton("Run")
bar.add_action(run_button)

    bar.set_progress(state["done"], total, unit="ligands")
    if state["done"] == total:
        timer.stop()
        bar.finish("Done", f"{total} ligands docked")


def start():

    bar.start("Docking…")
    timer.start()


timer.timeout.connect(tick)
run_button.clicked.connect(start)

panel.resize(420, 360)

items.title: Alcance del baseline
items.text:
Este baseline describe el estado real de src/molsuite_components/ms_monitor/ en el código actual, con foco en:

  • fuentes de datos
  • acoplamientos
  • superficie pública del bridge
  • capacidades realmente disponibles
  • riesgos estructurales inmediatos

No describe el objetivo futuro del monitor. Describe lo que hoy existe.

items.title: Estructura actual
items.text:
ms_monitor tiene 1307 líneas en 12 módulos Python.

Distribución principal:

  • polling.py: 354 líneas
  • widget.py: 288 líneas
  • bridge.py: 116 líneas
  • models.py: 113 líneas
  • resto de módulos: 12 a 96 líneas

Lectura pragmática:

  • la estructura de archivos es razonable
  • la complejidad real está concentrada en polling.py y widget.py
  • el problema actual no es monolito por tamaño, sino contrato y acoplamiento

items.title: Fuente primaria

El poller usa principalmente una instancia de MolSuite:

  • molsuite.get_runtime_healthcheck()
  • molsuite.executor_manager.get_status()

  • molsuite.get_job_outputs(job_id) como fallback

La cancelación actual va directa al manager:

  • molsuite.executor_manager.cancel_job(job_id)

MolSuiteMonitorBridge expone hoy:

  • start()
  • stop()
  • refresh_now()
  • get_recent_events(job_id=None)
  • get_recent_outputs(job_id, limit=...)
  • cancel_job(job_id)

Señales Qt:

  • job_upserted
  • job_removed
  • job_finished
  • executors_updated
  • health_updated

items.title: Modelos actuales

El monitor ya tiene modelos dataclass tipados:

  • ProjectMonitorState
  • JobMonitorState
  • ChunkMonitorState
  • EventMonitorState
  • ExecutorMonitorState
  • RuntimeHealthState

Eso es una buena base. El problema no es falta de modelos, sino que gran parte del poller sigue normalizando desde dict crudos del runtime en línea.

items.title: Acoplamientos aceptables
items.text:
• dependencia del monitor en MolSuite
  • dependencia del widget en el bridge y en modelos tipados
  • uso de señales Qt para desacoplar polling y UI

items.title: Acoplamientos a reducir
items.text:
• polling.py depende directo de executor_manager
  • polling.py depende de shapes crudos de get_status(), list_jobs() y get_job()
  • bridge.cancel_job() depende directo de executor_manager
  • bridge.get_recent_outputs() mezcla dos rutas de acceso sin contrato formal del orden de preferencia

items.title: Síntoma práctico
items.text: El monitor ya no está acoplado a SQL crudo, pero todavía depende demasiado de shapes del runtime que no están formalizados como contrato específico para monitor.

items.title: Uso actual de datos crudos
items.text:
Hoy el monitor trata respuestas crudas de dict en varios puntos:

  • health_raw.get(...)
  • status_raw.get(...)
  • item.get(...) para executors
  • summary.get(...) para jobs resumidos
  • raw.get(...) para detalle de job

Eso no rompe funcionalidad, pero vuelve frágil la evolución del monitor porque el contrato efectivo vive implícito dentro de polling.py.

items.title: Estado funcional actual

Lo que sí funciona hoy:

  • detectar ausencia de proyecto activo
  • detectar cambio de proyecto
  • construir snapshot del proyecto activo
  • mostrar jobs del proyecto activo
  • mostrar health del runtime
  • mostrar resumen de executors
  • mostrar chunks vivos
  • mostrar eventos recientes
  • mostrar outputs recientes
  • refresco manual
  • cancelación básica desde UI

La suite tests/test_molsuite_monitor_bridge.py ya cubre lo esencial:

  • staging y chunks vivos
  • cancelación observada
  • orden de jobs activos y terminales recientes
  • eventos recientes por job

Lectura pragmática:

  • la deuda está más en el contrato y en las acciones de operador que en la ausencia total de comportamiento

items.text:
• que cambios en shapes internos del runtime rompan polling.py
  • que la cancelación siga atada a internals en vez de una ruta soportada
  • que outputs, eventos y logs se mezclen semánticamente
  • que el historial crezca sin política explícita
  • que AMDock termine consumiendo detalles no canónicos del bridge

items.title: Conclusión
items.text:
ms_monitor ya es usable como monitor básico. No está “roto” en lo esencial.

Lo que falta no es rehacerlo desde cero, sino formalizarlo:

  • contrato de datos del monitor
  • contrato de capacidades soportadas
  • reducción del acoplamiento a executor_manager
  • separación más clara entre observar, diagnosticar y actuar

items.title: Politica de acciones de operador en ms_monitor
path: Politica de acciones de operador en ms_monitor

items.title: Objetivo
items.text:
Definir qué acciones de operador están soportadas hoy por ms_monitor, con qué contrato, y qué acciones quedan explícitamente fuera.

La regla es simple:

  • solo se soportan acciones con backend claro y semántica defendible
  • lo no soportado se declara como tal
  • la UI no debe inventar mutaciones que el runtime no garantiza

items.text:

  • diagnosticar
  • ejecutar un conjunto pequeño de acciones seguras

items.title: Guided tutorials
items.text: ms_components.ms_tutorial supplies informative and interactive tours for any Qt Widgets application. It imports no application, project catalog, or orchestrator. No existing application slot needs a tutorial call.

items.title: Python bindings, optional TOML content
items.text:
Use Python for widget/signal bindings. They are live Qt objects and may need application logic to reveal a panel or verify a result. Use either Python or TOML for tutorial content. Both produce the same Tutorial model.

TOML is useful when editing explanations or translating a tour without touching bindings. It uses Python 3.12's standard-library tomllib, so no YAML dependency is needed. Files contain symbolic IDs, never Python expressions, imports, widget attribute paths, or executable callbacks. Unknown keys and invalid definitions raise ValueError; TOML syntax and filesystem errors propagate to the caller.

id = "first-import"
title = "Import your data"

[[steps]]
id = "overview"
target = "input.panel"
title = "Input panel"
text = "Configure your input here, then review the resulting records."

[[steps]]
id = "import"
target = "input.run"
title = "Import the example"
text = "Run the import. This step advances only after the expected job succeeds."
advance_on = "input.imported"

from ms_components.ms_tutorial import (
    TutorialController, TutorialEvent, TutorialTarget, load_tutorial,
)

window.tutorials = TutorialController(
    targets={
        "input.panel": TutorialTarget(lambda: window.input_panel,
                                      prepare=window.show_input_panel),
        "input.run": TutorialTarget(lambda: window.input_panel.run_button),
    },
    events={
        "input.imported": TutorialEvent(
            window.monitor_bridge.job_finished,
            accept=lambda job_id, status: job_id == expected_job_id() and status == "completed",
        ),
    },
    parent=window,
)
window.tutorials.start(load_tutorial("first_import.toml"))

Names such as input.panel are plain dictionary keys. The application supplies their meaning; ms_tutorial knows nothing about AMDockVS or Molsuite's job statuses. The example's expected_job_id() and show_input_panel are application-provided functions, not methods required by this component. Real operations still go through the application's existing APIs.

For a small tour, define the content in Python instead:

from ms_components.ms_tutorial import Tutorial, TutorialStep

overview = Tutorial("overview", "Interface overview", (
    TutorialStep("input", "input.panel", "Input", "Configure your data here."),
    TutorialStep("run", "input.run", "Run", "This submits the configured operation."),
))
window.tutorials.start(overview)

items.title: Informative and interactive steps
items.text:
• Without advance_on, a step is informative: Next/Back control the tour. The spotlight remains visible but blocks clicks and keyboard actions on the host window. The component never clicks controls or executes application actions.
  • With advance_on, a step is interactive: the spotlight admits real input to its target, and Next stays disabled until the named event is accepted. Completion advances automatically. Other application slots retain their existing connections.
  • TutorialEvent.accept receives the signal's arguments. Use it to match the job, project, selection, or success state that the step actually expects. A request or button click does not in general prove that an asynchronous operation succeeded.
  • Events are observed only while their step is active. Already completed steps may be revisited with Back and left with Next. A new run resets tutorial completion, without resetting application data. Multiple queued copies of an old event do not complete a later step, even if both steps use the same signal.

For asynchronous operations that may finish while the user has gone Back, supply TutorialEvent(signal, accept=..., is_complete=lambda: cached_result_is_ready). The controller checks is_complete when entering an unfinished step and advances if it returns true. The application records successful completion before emitting its signal; the callback reads that state, without blocking or querying a database. accept validates incoming signal arguments; is_complete independently checks the operation and result that the step requires.

TutorialEvent.signal also accepts a zero-argument resolver for signals belonging to dialogs or controls that are recreated. It is resolved when entering the step.

The controller queues event validation to the UI thread, including signals emitted by background workers. Validators must be fast and must not mutate the UI or start another tutorial. Signal argument types must be supported by Qt's queued connections (Python objects and the ordinary Qt types are suitable).

items.title: Dynamic panels and multiple windows
items.text:
TutorialTarget.widget is a QWidget or a zero-argument resolver returning one. Optional TutorialTarget.rect resolves a rectangle in that widget's coordinates, for example rect=lambda: menu_bar.actionGeometry(help_action) to highlight just the Help menu item. It is recomputed as the layout changes; the widget is unchanged. The controller resolves it again as the UI changes. prepare, when provided, runs once on entering the step and should only reveal the needed UI, through its existing public navigation API. Do not submit jobs or change scientific data there. Navigation callbacks must also account for Back, for example hiding a modal dialog when returning to its parent window; the controller does not close application dialogs.

An overlay belongs to the target's top-level window. On the next step the controller can move to another window, a floating dock, or a modal dialog, without application slots knowing about it. It follows resizing, moving, and ancestor viewport clipping. Use prepare to scroll offscreen controls into view; the component does not scroll the application automatically. Hidden targets temporarily hide the overlay; an initial hidden target without an existing overlay fails with a diagnostic. Missing or deleted targets and callback failures stop the tour and emit failed.

Call the public controller.refresh() after an application UI change when the spotlight should update immediately. Normal tracking continues automatically. Accepting a host QDialog preserves the tutorial so its target can move back to the parent window; closing or rejecting the host still cancels the tutorial.

For tutorials where every step advances through an application event, TutorialController(close_only=True) replaces the Back, Next and Exit buttons with a compact close button in the callout header. Escape still cancels. Every step must provide advance_on; starting a close-only tutorial with an informational step raises ValueError, since there would be no way to advance. The default controls remain available for informative tours.

TutorialController(dim_background=False) preserves the application's background colors and draws only the target outline. Input gating remains the same. instruction_provider=lambda step: current_instruction supplies dynamic plain-text instructions. They are measured again only when their text changes, without resetting the reader's scroll position on every tracking tick. These options do not depend on any application or project package.

Lifecycle signals:

Signal Arguments started tutorial ID step_changed step ID, zero-based index finished tutorial ID cancelled tutorial ID failed tutorial ID, diagnostic message

Call start(tutorial), next(), back(), or stop() on the UI thread. Keep the controller alive, normally as an attribute of the main window, and give it a Qt parent. Escape/Exit cancel; closing the current host also cancels. Stopping a tour removes its signal connection and event filter and restores the earlier focus when that widget is still visible. Switching tutorials cancels the previous one. Invalid target/event registry keys are rejected before cancelling an active tour. The component never creates QApplication or changes the application's theme.

items.title: Demo and checks
items.text:
From the source checkout, in MSDD_312:

PYTHONPATH=src python examples/tutorial_demo.py
QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen PYTHONPATH=src python -m pytest -q tests/test_tutorial.py

The demo has two buttons: an informative tour defined in Python, and a mixed interactive/informative tour loaded from examples/tutorial_demo.toml. Its application slot has no tutorial calls. Add the sibling ms_flow/src and ms_env/src to PYTHONPATH if those packages are not installed in the environment.

items.title: Scope
items.text: This component guides an existing UI within one process. Continuing in a new process, saving progress, translation catalogs, and the application's Help menu remain the application's responsibility. A spotlight over native platform dialogs or embedded OpenGL renderers is platform-dependent; use a Qt Widgets practice view if needed. On a host almost entirely occupied by the target, the callout may overlap part of the spotlight. Expose a smaller target in the binding to leave room for the callout.

items.title: Project form events
items.text:
ProjectsMenuWidget and ProjectBrowserPanel emit project_form_opened(ProjectFormDialog) before entering a create/edit form's modal loop. The form's mode is "create" or "edit". Hosts can bind controls and observe the normal accepted, rejected, and finished Qt signals without searching the browser's widget tree or replacing its actions.

ProjectFormDialog is exported from ms_components.ms_projects. Its public controls include name_input, path_input, path_row, browse_button, and save_button. name_committed(str) emits the trimmed name when editing finishes. path_selected(str) emits only when Browse confirms a folder, including selecting the current folder again. Cancelling the chooser emits no selection event.

project_created(project_id) means that project creation succeeded. It remains separate from opening the form or accepting its fields, which may still be followed by a backend error. None of these APIs depend on ms_tutorial or a host application.

items.title: API guide
items.text: Every component is a plain PySide6 widget. Create a QApplication first, pass dependencies through the constructor, and apply the theme once.

items.title: Theme
items.text:
apply_theme() sets the palette and the base stylesheet for the whole application, and re-applies them live to existing widgets.

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication

from ms_components.theme import THEMES, apply_theme, color, font, set_base_font

app = QApplication([])
set_base_font(10.0, app=app)
apply_theme("auto", app)     # or a name from THEMES, e.g. "nord"

print(sorted(THEMES))
warning = color("orange")    # semantic accent from the live theme
title_font = font("title")

Widgets should read colours from the palette (palette(window), palette(highlight), …) instead of hard-coded hex values, so they follow theme changes. Non-Qt views such as PyMOL or pyqtgraph do not observe the palette and must be updated separately.

items.title: SmartTableView
items.text:
Define a SQLModel model, describe the columns, and provide a session provider. The table handles querying, filtering, sorting, and pagination.

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QApplication
from sqlmodel import Field, Session, SQLModel, create_engine

from ms_components.ms_table import ColumnDef, SmartTableView, TableConfig


class Molecule(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    name: str
    score: float | None = None


class Database:
    def __init__(self, engine):
        self.engine = engine

    def get_session(self) -> Session:
        return Session(self.engine)


app = QApplication([])
engine = create_engine("sqlite:///molecules.db")
SQLModel.metadata.create_all(engine)

table = SmartTableView(
    db=Database(engine),
    config=TableConfig(
        model_class=Molecule,
        columns=[
            ColumnDef("id", label="ID", width=70),
            ColumnDef("name", label="Molecule", filterable=True),
            ColumnDef("score", label="Score", sortable=True),
        ],
        page_size=50,
    ),
)
table.row_double_clicked.connect(lambda molecule: print(molecule.id))
table.resize(800, 500)
table.show()
app.exec()

Call refresh() or refresh_preserving_view() after external data changes. Filters imposed by the application go through set_external_filters() or set_external_clause(), which keeps them apart from the filters the user edits.

items.title: ToolPanel
items.text:
ToolPanel is the frame shared by configure-then-run tools: an optional top bar, a scrolling body of sections, and an action bar. It knows nothing about jobs; the host maps its job events onto the action bar.

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QPushButton, QSpinBox

from ms_components.tool_panel import ToolPanel

panel = ToolPanel()

options = panel.add_section("Options", description="Docking parameters")
options.add_row("Exhaustiveness", QSpinBox())

panel.advanced.add_row("Seed", QSpinBox())   # collapsed section kept last

bar = panel.action_bar
bar.add_action(QPushButton("Run"))
bar.set_summary("120 ligands selected")

bar.start("Docking…")
bar.set_progress(40, 120, unit="ligands")
bar.finish("Done", "120 ligands docked")

ToolSection.add_row() accepts the QFormLayout.addRow overloads: (label, field), a single spanning widget, or a layout.

items.title: QStepper
items.text:
QStepper shows a sequence of steps. add_step() returns a QStep, which is a widget you fill with content.

from PySide6.QtWidgets import QLabel

from ms_components.ms_stepper import QStepper

stepper = QStepper()
first = stepper.add_step("Input", "Choose the files")
first.add_widget(QLabel("Select ligands and receptors."))
second = stepper.add_step("Run", "Start the job")
second.add_widget(QLabel("Review and run."))

stepper.current_changed.connect(lambda index: print("step", index))
stepper.finished.connect(lambda: print("finished"))

Pass a validator to QStep to block advancing until its content is valid. Inside a stepper, put one ToolPanel per step so each step keeps its own action bar state.

items.title: Job monitor
items.text:
The bridge polls an ms_flow Workspace and translates its snapshots into Qt signals and models; the widget only presents them. You can embed the whole monitor or consume only the bridge signals.

from ms_flow import Workspace
from ms_components.ms_monitor import MolSuiteMonitorBridge, MolSuiteMonitorWidget

ms = Workspace(app_id="demo")
ms.create_or_open_project(name="demo", folder="./demo-project", activate=True)

bridge = MolSuiteMonitorBridge(workspace=ms, poll_ms=500)
monitor = MolSuiteMonitorWidget(bridge=bridge)
bridge.bridge_error.connect(print)
bridge.job_finished.connect(lambda job_id, status: print("job finished", job_id, status))
bridge.start()
monitor.show()

When closing, call bridge.stop() first and ms.shutdown() afterwards. The operator can cancel jobs, Resume a job that was interrupted or canceled, and Move a job to another active executor. An application with its own rules of where a job may go passes resume(job_id, executor) and destinations(job_id) to the bridge.

items.title: Where jobs run
items.text:
ms_components.ms_executors edits the hosts and executors kept by ms_flow. Both widgets go through the Workspace, which refuses what cannot be done now (changing an executor while it is active, for example) and says why.

from ms_components.ms_executors import ExecutorsPanel, KeptPage

hosts = KeptPage(ms, "hosts")            # a Settings page: the machines
executors = KeptPage(ms, "executors")    # a Settings page: who runs jobs on them
panel = ExecutorsPanel(ms)               # the quick window that starts and stops executors
panel.settings_requested.connect(lambda: print("open the Settings page"))
panel.show()

items.title: Projects, settings, and PyMOL
items.text:
Applications embedding PyMOL should call ms_components.opengl.prepare_pymol_opengl() before creating QApplication. It requests desktop OpenGL and shared contexts, then checks the actual context and compiles legacy GLSL shaders in an isolated process. A failed native check can select xcb on Linux only when an X11 display passes the same check and QT_QPA_PLATFORM was not explicitly set. Windows and macOS retain their native platforms. If no tested backend works, it raises RuntimeError before the application starts. Skip this call when PyMOL is disabled or running headlessly.

PymolDockWidget also requests desktop OpenGL on its own widget and validates the actual context before drawing. An incompatible context displays an error in the viewer instead of passing it to PyMOL.

  • ProjectsMenuWidget(app_id=...) and ProjectBrowserWindow(app_id=...) list and create projects through the public ms_flow project catalog. Connect project_requested to open the chosen project; do not read the MolSuite databases from the UI.
  • AppSettingsDialog(runtime=...) edits the layered configuration of an application.
  • PymolDockWidget(title, manager) needs the PyMOL cmd/manager object of the application's PyMOL integration.
